posts.author: Blitz_Burgh@sportsbots.xyz
posts.text: Sports Illustrated’s Gilberto Manzano still thinks the Steelers aren’t real: “Don’t be fooled by Pittsburgh’s three-game winning streak. That shouldn’t be enough to believe this will be the year the Steelers end their seven-game playoff losing streak. Yes, there’s plenty to like about Pittsburgh’s positive stretch. The defense has been outstanding the past two weeks, and that unit was enough to overcome an up-and-down outing from Aaron Rodgers and his offense in the win over the Saints. Rodgers was better in the wins against the Colts and Buccaneers, but that’s three victories against a trio of teams that have two wins apiece. Perhaps I’ll start falling for the Steelers again if Rodgers outpaces Joe Burrow a second time and the defense shuts down the pesky Browns after the Week 4 loss. But for now, the Steelers’ three-game winning streak is misleading because they’ve faced three losing teams. Don’t trust them just yet.” #Steelers #NFL

posts.text: FOX Sports’ Ralph Vacchiano believes Jaylen Warren can carry the Steelers to the playoffs: “Over the past five weeks, running back Jaylen Warren has emerged as one of the NFL’s best and most elusive backs, and he’s the main reason the Steelers still sit tied atop the bruising AFC North. After shaking off a slow start — he amassed just 89 rushing yards and 61 receiving yards over the first two weeks — Warren has been on a heater. And after adding 101 rushing yards and three catches for 36 yards on Sunday morning in Paris against the New Orleans Saints, he’s now averaging 94.4 rushing yards and 141 total yards over the past five games. In short, Warren is giving the Steelers the power and the explosiveness they desperately need. Warren is the reason Rodgers’ last ride has a chance to finish with the 14th playoff berth of his Hall of Fame career.” #Steelers #NFL

posts.author: tompelissero.bsky.social
posts.text:
Bucs QB Baker Mayfield underwent tests that showed no fracture and no tendon or ligament damage in his right thumb, sources tell The Ringer and Netflix Sports. 

Mayfield will need to regain strength after Sunday’s dislocation and likely will miss some time. But good news overall.

posts.author: tompelissero.bsky.social
posts.text:
By trading J.J. McCarthy now, the Vikings save over $4.6M in cash and cap space and get an unconditional fifth-round pick in the next draft that, depending how the Giants finish, could end up being a top-150 selection.

Meanwhile, New York adds another former first-round pick QB.

posts.author: tompelissero.bsky.social
posts.text:
Trade! The Vikings are sending QB J.J. McCarthy to the Giants for a 2027 fifth-round pick, sources tell The Ringer and Netflix Sports.

With Jaxson Dart out for the regular season, New York adds another young QB, while Minnesota gains flexibility and McCarthy gets a fresh start.
